case_name: Chandraprakash Madhavrao Dadwa and Others v Union of India and Others
facts: The petitioners, who fall under (1) above filed SLP (C) No. 16646 of 1995, questioning their redesignation as Data Entry Operators.

The appellants are 48 in number and have all been directly recruited in 1978 and thereafter as "Data Processing Assistants" in the scale of Rs. 330-560 in the Data Processing Division of the National Sample Survey Organisation (hereinafter called the NSSO), Department of Statistics, Ministry of Planning, Government of India.
The appellants put on several years of service as Data Processing Assistants from various dates after 1978 and in the year 1990, the impugned order dated 2-7-1990 was passed.
The officers who were immediately above the appellants namely Data Processing Supervisors as well as the appellants, Data Processing Assistants moved the Central Administrative Tribunal.
This SLP was initially dismissed on 1-9-1995. Now the SLP has been restored by allowing Review Petition No. 2096 of 1995.
issues: Whether the redesignation of the petitioners as Data Entry Operators Grade B and giving them a lower scale is bad in law.
Whether the administrative order dated 2-7-1990 was not inconsistent with the Rules of 1977 or 1978.
petitioner_arguments: The appellants were directly recruited in NSSO under the statutory Rules of 1977 as Data Processing Assistants and they were in the course of time entitled under the 1978 Rules to be "promoted" as Data Processing Supervisors.

A person directly recruited to a post could not be shifted to a post which was not in the Rules but was in a different stream carrying scales inferior to the one to which the appellants were entitled, i.e., Rs. 1600-2660 in the Data Processing stream.
respondent_arguments: The administrative order dated 2-7-1990 fixed slightly higher essential qualifications which the appellants did not possess.

Data Processing Assistants like the appellants in the scale of Rs. 1200-2040 were, therefore, rightly brought into the Data Entry stream and redesignated as Data Entry Operators Grade B in the scale of Rs. 1350-2200.
court_reasoning: The shifting of the appellants to the Data Entry stream and the refusal to grant them the revised scale of Rs. 1600-2660 applicable to Data Processing Supervisors, was illegal.
Any change in the essential qualifications could only be prospective and should not affect those who were already recruited to the costs.
holding: We allow the review petition. The SLP is taken up and leave is granted. In fact, with the consent of counsel, the appeal itself has been heard as the parties have filed copies of the pleadings, documents and affidavits.
cases_cited: Chandraprakash Madhavrao Dadwa and Others v Union of India
